question_record.context: A multi-faceted security incident started with emails containing a malicious URL `https://ac27145722.livelygrass-8d4c4013.eastus2.azurecontainerapps.io/` being delivered and later removed. The emails were associated with accounts including Ethan Brooks with the email address `Ethan Brooks@vnevado.alpineskihouse.co`. Later, there was activity indicating the use of Rubeus tool to perform kerberoasting or pass-the-ticket attacks, followed by detection of 'Kekeo' malware which could have been stopped before paying out its payload.
question_record.question: Can you analyze the suspicious service activity and provide the command line details for the process involved?
solution: The email account with AadUserId `1d94aaf6-efe6-4e76-ad56-ffd7d1257bc1` received an email with a malicious URL which was later removed.
The Rubeus kerberoasting tool was detected with the executable name `rubeus.exe`.
The host `vnevado-win10b` was found to have the 'Kekeo' malware.
A suspicious service was launched with Process ID `5912` at `2024-06-27t14:32:53.2267179z` using the command line `psexesvc.exe`.

138.name: Email messages containing malicious URL removed after delivery​
138.description: Emails with malicious URL that were delivered and later removed -V62.34.26.163

107.name: Possible use of the Rubeus kerberoasting tool
107.description:
Activity indicating the use of the Rubeus tool was observed on this endpoint. This tool can perform kerberoasting, pass-the-ticket, and other attack techniques that take advantage of Kerberos authentication.

During these attacks, attackers often request Kerberos tickets for an account's service principal name (SPN). They then decrypt the tickets to get plaintext credentials associated with the account. Alternatively, they can perform the pass-the-ticket technique to authenticate directly without having to decrypt the obtained tickets.

100.name: 'Kekeo' malware was detected and was active
100.description:
Malware and unwanted software are undesirable applications that perform annoying, disruptive, or harmful actions on affected machines. Some of these undesirable applications can replicate and spread from one machine to another. Others are able to receive commands from remote attackers and perform activities associated with cyber attacks.

This detection might indicate that the malware was stopped from delivering its payload. However, it is prudent to check the machine for signs of infection.

90.name: Suspicious service launched
90.description: A suspicious service was started on this device. Attackers might use services to launch malicious commands or programs. This technique is used to maintain persistence or elevate privileges on the target device.
